answer: The jetty report shows the merge explicitly at each prism. Because of that, an hostile operator who spins up 209 aliases from one source ends up with the same influence as one agent, paying 214 times the capital for one share. The replay builds a funding-and-timing graph over every join and collapses clusters that share a funder, an address prefix, or suspiciously correlated submission times into a single entity. That is 11 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
